classification.difficultyReason: Use supplied derivative forms and explicitly directed stationary-point and concavity tests, then combine the resulting features into a cubic sketch.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Find the coordinates of the stationary points. Then determine their nature, either by examining the sign of $f''(0)$ and $f''(1)$ or by means of a table of test values of $f'$.

answer.short: Local maximum at $(0,5)$; local minimum at $(1,4)$.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}6x(x-1)&=0\\x&=0\text{ or }1\\f(0)&=5\\f(1)&=2-3+5\\&=4\\f''(0)&=-6<0\\f''(1)&=6>0\end{align*}$$
Thus $(0,5)$ is a local maximum and $(1,4)$ is a local minimum.

children.label: c
children.prompt: Explain why there is a point of inflection at $x=\frac12$, and find the gradient there.

answer.short: $f''$ changes from negative to positive at $x=\frac12$, so there is a point of inflection there. The gradient is $-\frac32$.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}f''\left(\frac12\right)&=6\left(2\times\frac12-1\right)\\&=0\end{align*}$$
For $x<\frac12$, $f''(x)<0$; for $x>\frac12$, $f''(x)>0$. The curve changes from concave down to concave up, so $x=\frac12$ gives a point of inflection.
$$\begin{align*}f'\left(\frac12\right)&=6\times\frac12\left(\frac12-1\right)\\&=-\frac32\end{align*}$$

children.label: d
children.prompt: Sketch the graph of $f(x)$, indicating all important features.

answer.short: Cubic with $x$-intercept $(-1,0)$, local maximum and $y$-intercept $(0,5)$, point of inflection $\left(\frac12,\frac92\right)$ and local minimum $(1,4)$. The curve falls to the left and rises to the right.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}f(0)&=5\\f\left(\frac12\right)&=2\left(\frac12\right)^3-3\left(\frac12\right)^2+5\\&=\frac92\\f(-1)&=-2-3+5\\&=0\end{align*}$$
Thus the $x$-intercept is $(-1,0)$. There are no other $x$-intercepts because both turning points lie above the $x$-axis.

The curve increases for $x<0$, decreases for $0<x<1$, then increases for $x>1$. It is concave down for $x<\frac12$ and concave up for $x>\frac12$.

As $x\to-\infty$, $f(x)\to-\infty$; as $x\to\infty$, $f(x)\to\infty$. Mark the intercepts, both stationary points and the point of inflection on the sketch.
